</defs><rect width="340" height="110" fill="#fff"/><rect x="10" y="20" width="120" height="70" fill="#fff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="70.0" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#222">Vehicle</text><line x1="10" y1="50" x2="130" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="16" y="66" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">-speed: double</text><text x="16" y="82" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">+move(): void</text><rect x="210" y="20" width="120" height="70" fill="#fff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="270.0" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#222">Car</text><line x1="210" y1="50" x2="330" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="216" y="66" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">-doors: int</text><text x="216" y="82" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">+start(): void</text><line x1="210" y1="62" x2="130" y2="62" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#tri)"/></svg>
options: Car merely uses Vehicle as a local variable.
Car and Vehicle have no type relationship.
explanation: A solid line with a hollow triangle is generalisation (inheritance), and the triangle points at the superclass. Here it touches Vehicle, so Car extends Vehicle and gets speed and move() as well as its own doors and start(). Option A reverses the direction. The arrow always points from the child to the parent. A 'local variable' use (C) would be a dashed dependency arrow.

options: Every Task belongs to exactly one Project.
Every Project has exactly one Task.
A Task can belong to multiple Projects.
explanation: Read each multiplicity at the FAR end. The '1' next to Project tells you how many Projects one Task is linked to (exactly one). The '1..*' next to Task tells you how many Tasks one Project has (one or more). So A is correct. B is the classic mistake of reading the '1' from the wrong side. C contradicts the '1', and D contradicts the '1..*' (at least one).

</defs><rect width="340" height="118" fill="#fff"/><rect x="10" y="20" width="120" height="78" fill="#fff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="70.0" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#222">Order</text><line x1="10" y1="50" x2="130" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="16" y="66" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">-orderId: int</text><line x1="10" y1="74" x2="130" y2="74" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="16" y="90" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">+total(): double</text><rect x="210" y="20" width="120" height="78" fill="#fff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="270.0" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#222">OrderLine</text><line x1="210" y1="50" x2="330" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="216" y="66" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">-quantity: int</text><line x1="210" y1="74" x2="330" y2="74" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="216" y="90" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">+subtotal(): double</text><line x1="210" y1="61" x2="130" y2="61" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#dfill)"/><text x="160" y="54" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#bf8700" font-weight="bold">1</text><text x="194" y="54" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#bf8700" font-weight="bold">1..*</text></svg>
options: Order is the composite whole of its OrderLines.
explanation: A filled (black) diamond is composition, and the diamond sits at the WHOLE. Order owns its OrderLines: they cannot be shared with another Order, and they are destroyed when the Order is. In Java, Order usually creates them itself. The multiplicities say an Order has 1..* lines and each line belongs to exactly 1 Order. A hollow diamond would be the weaker aggregation. D describes a dependency (dashed arrow).

options: Team aggregates Members; they may exist independently.
Team creates a local Member only once.
explanation: A hollow (white) diamond is aggregation, a weak whole–part ('has-a') relationship with the diamond at the whole. A Team holds 0..* Members, but those Members exist independently: they are usually passed in through add(m) rather than created inside Team, and they survive if the Team is deleted. Compare Q14: a FILLED diamond means composition, where the parts' lifetime is owned. D describes a dependency, not aggregation.

</defs><rect width="340" height="148" fill="#fff"/><rect x="10" y="20" width="120" height="78" fill="#fff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="70.0" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#222">Teacher</text><line x1="10" y1="50" x2="130" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="16" y="66" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">-id: int</text><line x1="10" y1="74" x2="130" y2="74" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="16" y="90" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">+getId(): int</text><rect x="210" y="20" width="120" height="78" fill="#fff" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="270.0" y="40" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#222">Course</text><line x1="210" y1="50" x2="330" y2="50" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="216" y="66" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">-code: String</text><line x1="210" y1="74" x2="330" y2="74" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="216" y="90" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222">+getCode(): String</text><line x1="130" y1="61" x2="210" y2="61" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#open)"/><text x="170" y="53" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#1f6feb" font-weight="bold">teaches</text><text x="138" y="79" text-anchor="start" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222" font-weight="bold">1</text><text x="202" y="79" text-anchor="end" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#222" font-weight="bold">0..*</text><text x="170" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#555">Solid association with navigability toward Course</text></svg>
options: Each Course has 1 Teacher; a Teacher has 0..* Courses.
Each Teacher has 1 Course; a Course has 0..* Teachers.
Course is a subclass of Teacher.
Teacher owns Course objects by composition.
explanation: This is a plain solid association with an open arrowhead for navigability: Teacher can reach its Courses (it would hold a Course collection), but not the other way. Read multiplicities at the far end. The '0..*' at Course means one Teacher teaches 0..* Courses, and the '1' at Teacher means each Course has exactly 1 Teacher. B is the reversed reading. There is no triangle (so not C) and no filled diamond (so not D).
